chapter: Touring shows and the bands he heard
title: Drummer Old Man Joe White and the Rotisserie
summary: Old Man Joe White, parade drummer with the Rabbit Foot Minstrels, led street parades and demanded supper at every gig.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: These different guys had these different qualities. Like Old Man Joe White who played the drums. I played with him at a place called the Rotisserie -- that was out in

North Jackson. He was quite a character. I used to play some gigs with him in different places. But the Rotisserie was like another type of Pig-Stand, but only more classy, out in North Jackson, where there was... He liked to play at the White section, and we'd play out there.
You still got a pork sandwich there.

Right, right, right. But they served other things, too. And during that period, I had fallen on roller skates and broken my arm, and I was playing with him at the Rotisserie with my arm in a cast, you know. I had some great times playing with him. He was quite an experience. A great personality, this man, you know...
You were describing him before we started taping.

Right. He was the drummer with the Rabbit Foot Minstrel Show. And he used to lead the parades. See, when the minstrel shows came to town, they would parade through the city, drumming up business for that night's performance. And he would lead the band. Well, you've never seen anybody who play a parade drum the way he could play one. And he could roll a drum than anybody I've ever heard. And I've heard Elvin Jones and Art Blakey roll it, but they were no way in his league when it comes to making a roll...or press roll on that parade drum. He was fantastic, and he had a great personality, because he could do all

kinds of things with the sticks and everything, you know... Now and then, I would work a gig maybe out in some of those little towns or somewhere locally with him. And he always made one stipulation in his agreement. Besides the money, they would have to have supper! [LAUGHS] No gigs that didn't include supper.

And they tell me he's still living at home now, and he's kind of senile, you know. But the man was a great, great personality, and a great character, and a great drummer. You know, he was really something to see. He was a big attraction... He was an attraction. When he started coming down the street, it was beautiful to see him strutting, and with all the kind of pride in what he was doing... Oh, it was really beautiful.
